fixed.item: breakages.json (electrical's request): spills and splashes from plumbing's own verbs never reached the kernel's wetting hooks (common.wet wrote wetness directly; T-686df131c7c736-01 seed 1: coffee maker, microwave and toaster at wetness 0.5, a breaker trip 8 s later read as exogenous)
fixed.how: common.wet(w, eid, liters, liquid, source) is now house_sim.kernel.phys.liquids.wet (film model / saturation; every phys.wetted hook sees the litres and the source). Every wetting of the domain passes the litres that reach the thing: a spill on a surface reaches what stands on it by its footprint's share of the top (common.share_on: the spill's expected liquid at the base, never more than the spill), a pour over a non-holder all of it and a container's contents their share (transfer.reached_contents), a tap stream splashes min(0.3 x the outer film, 10 ml) (transfer.FILL_SPLASH_*), a shaken drink sprays a quarter of its spray onto what the other hand holds (liquids.split_parcel, conserved), a basin overflow runs down its cabinet (fixtures.overflow), a tilted ice tray onto its shelf (ice.tray_placed), drips onto what they land on (leaks.drip_onto; gear and water_safe=false things are no drip catchers whatever their case, leaks._water_sensitive) and a hose spray onto its target (outdoor.rinse_entity, which still leaves the faces it hit drenched). Water damage of a water-sensitive thing now needs common.WATER_DAMAGE_L = 0.02 L (electrical's INGRESS_L) to reach or gather on it: a glug's few ml beside appliances wets them a little and damages nothing; a litre run over the counter damages them (and electrical's hook trips the GFCI or flags the shock risk, attributed to the robot).

fixed.item: Performance (P1 gate G7 regressed 3.21 -> 3.85 ms/substep): this domain's systems
fixed.how: Measured first: on one frozen tree (HEAD kernel and other domains) the ADOPT and phase-1 plumbing files cost nearly the same (bench loop, plumbing systems summed, best of 3 interleaved rounds: 0.365 vs 0.376 ms/substep), so about +0.01 of the gate's +0.031 for plumbing (water 0.266 -> 0.290, slow 0.040 -> 0.047) was this domain's code; now 0.334, below ADOPT. Exact reductions anyway (perf): fixtures.tap_state reads the supply factors and tank only when something can flow or drip; supply.line_factor tables the stop valves once per substep (supply._stop_factors; min is order-free); ice.freeze_step looks up the ambient only for water it may freeze, ice that may melt, a part-frozen holder or a tray clock (and ice imports kernel.physics once); liquids.displacement_l scans with one list comprehension. Exactness: 14,160 randomised comparisons of line_factor and tap_state against the phase-1 implementations (0 mismatches) and 60 state digests (bench loop 40 substeps and a 1 h wait, 6 seeds x quiet / taps open / worn washers / main shut / water in the freezer) identical between the fix tree with and without the perf hunks.

T-686df131c7c736-01 (no edit): the two splashing wrong plans ('pours fast from the full carton', 'pours with the carton's spout on the low side') no longer carry 'damage' (labels damage+spills -> spills) on all 5 seeds: the glug's few ml on the counter now reach each appliance by its footprint's share and stay below the 0.02 L water-damage line (electrical's request; physically a splash beside a toaster does not water-damage it). Verdicts unchanged (PASS 5/5); every wrong plan still fails.

Whole catalog (frozen trees, HEAD vs HEAD + this domain's files, 243 specs x 5 seeds own mode, 51 realistic specs x 5 seeds --camera geometric): 0 verdict changes (1208/1215 and 250/255 on both sides: T-5a9598c809336a-01 and T-7d4006bda247ba-01 seeds 0/41 fail identically); the only wrong-plan label changes are the two rows above; reference end-state digests change in every spec (plunger size_m in every house).
perf: Measured with tools/bench_systems.py's loop (40 substeps x seeds 0-3, the plumbing systems summed; scratch abbench.py) on three frozen trees with the same kernel and other domains, interleaved, best of 3 rounds x 5 repeats (shared, heavily loaded machine): ADOPT plumbing files 0.365 ms/substep (water 0.309, slow 0.051, census 0.004); phase-1 plumbing (HEAD) 0.376 (water 0.320, slow 0.051, census 0.004); this change 0.334 (water 0.278, slow 0.052, census 0.004). So the domain's share of the G7 regression was about +0.01 ms (the gate's +0.031 for plumbing -- water 0.266 -> 0.290 -- was mostly the shared tree's load and kernel, same plumbing cost on one tree: 0.349-0.357 vs 0.356-0.360 in an earlier pair), and it is now 0.031 ms below ADOPT and 0.042 below phase 1 (water -13 %). Engine 1 h wait (env.step wait 3600 on seeds 0-3, idle probes on, systems timed inside the engine, mean of 3): plumbing 30.8 ms + 6.7 ms probe per hour -> 26.7 + 5.1 (about 0.31 -> 0.27 ms per 30 s substep); wall time of the four waits 1.360 -> 1.335 s (best of 3). Profile (steady state, substeps 2+): the cost is the per-tap tap_state (supply factors over every stop valve, the tank), freeze_step's ambient lookup per active holder, and a dripping worn tap's add/drain cycle (displacement scan, two write_states); the first two are now cheap, the third is real work. No result changed: 0 mismatches in 14,160 randomised line_factor / tap_state comparisons with the phase-1 code, identical state digests in 60 cases (bench loop and 1 h wait, 6 seeds x quiet / taps open / worn washers / main shut / water in the freezer) between the fix tree with and without the perf hunks, and the unit tests' probes-on/off digest test.
